tickets.title: Scope Exhaustion: The 'Silent' Failure
tickets.summary: Users in the Sales VLAN are intermittently failing to connect. Some have 169.254.x.x addresses.
artifact: Red Herring: DNS Server is pingable and healthy

triage.q: What is the first metric to check when users receive APIPA (169.254) addresses on a specific subnet?
options: Check if the DHCP Service is running on the DC
Verify the Scope Statistics for available address percentage
Restart the local switch for the Sales VLAN
Ping the default gateway from a working machine

diagnosis.q: The scope is 100% full with an 8-day lease. Why are new users failing even if old users have left for the day?
options: The addresses are still reserved by the server until the 8-day lease expires
The subnet mask is too long

fix.q: What is the best remediation to prevent this in a high-turnover environment?
options: Delete the scope and recreate it
Decrease the Lease Duration to 4 or 8 hours
Tell users to set static IP addresses

debrief.summary: Scope exhaustion is often caused by long lease times in mobile environments.
debrief.takeaway: Shortening leases allows the server to reclaim and reuse IPs more aggressively.
